deities: Lord Jambukeswarar (Shiva as the Appu/water lingam, swayambhu)
Goddess Akhilandeswari (Parvati, worshipped in a separate shrine)
festivals: Aadi Pooram (Goddess Akhilandeswari's special day, July-August)

history.dynasty: Early Chola (Kochenga Chola / Kocengannan); expanded by later Cholas, Pandyas, Vijayanagara and Nayaks
history.summary: Thiruvanaikaval is one of the five Pancha Bhoota Sthalams, representing the water element (neer): the sanctum of Jambukeswarar has a natural underground water stream and stays filled with water despite pumping. Built by Kochenga Chola (one of the 70 Madakkovils he is credited with) ~1,800 years ago, it is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams sung by all four Nayanars. Legend: Parvati, as Akhilandeswari, made a lingam from Kaveri water under the Venn Naaval tree and worshipped Shiva here; Shiva taught her Siva Gnana, making the temple a symbol of the guru-shishya relationship. An elephant worshipped here and was blessed — hence 'Thiruvanaikaval' (holy elephant temple). Five prakarams, the fifth ('Thiruneettan Thirumathil') said to have been built by Shiva himself in the form of a spider. Adi Shankaracharya is said to have installed Sri Chakra yantras as the goddess's ear ornaments to soften her radiance; priests dress as women in one daily ritual honouring Parvati's penance. OVERLAP NOTE: CSV seq 2255 ('Jambukeswarar Temple, Tiruchirappalli') is the SAME temple — this file (2244) is the primary record. CSV TOWN FLAG: actual town is Thiruvanaikaval on Srirangam island (~2 km from the Ranganathaswamy Temple), not 'Srirangam' town proper — documented with the corrected town.

name: Jambukeswarar Temple
town: Thiruvanaikaval (CSV town 'Srirangam' is approximate — the temple is at Thiruvanaikaval on Srirangam island, ~2 km from the Ranganathaswamy Temple)
town_description: Thiruvanaikaval is a temple neighbourhood on Srirangam island in Tiruchirappalli, between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers, near the city on the Trichy-Chennai highway. It is one of South India's most important Saivite pilgrimage sites and a well-known Paadal Petra Sthalam.
tradition: Shaivism (Pancha Bhoota water sthalam; Paadal Petra Sthalam)

travel.road: On the Trichy-Chennai highway, ~2 km from the Srirangam Ranganathaswamy Temple; auto-rickshaw, taxi and local bus (per vagabondinglife.in/airial)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Mondays are considered auspicious (per templeyatri.in); Panguni Brahmotsavam and Aadi Pooram are the major festival draws
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM-1:00 PM & 3:00-8:30 PM per livechennai.com/astroved.com; some sources give 4:00-9:00 PM for the evening (verify)
